messages:

Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Qualifying security posture & pen test handoff - MedSync

Hi Sylvia —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- You confirmed MedSync is pursuing HIPAA compliance and currently has a SOC 2 Type II report in progress (expected Q4 2027).
- Your security team wants our penetration test report, vulnerability management SLA (triage + remediation windows), and typical scanning cadence before legal proceeds.

Proposed next steps: 
1) I can share a redacted pen test report and our vuln-handling playbook with your security team.
2) If helpful, I’ll loop in our security ops lead to clarify SLA windows and scan cadence.
3) Agree scope for an NDA / limited data access for the report exchange.

Can you confirm the primary security contact (is Rajesh the right person for technical back-and-forth?) and whether a redacted report is sufficient initially?

Thanks —
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sales-one-pager.pdf (pdf)]
From: Sylvia Conrad <sylvia.conrad@medsync.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Qualifying security posture & pen test handoff - MedSync

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for the summary and for the call. Correct — Rajesh (cc'd) is our security engineering lead and will own technical reviews. A redacted penetration test report is fine to start; we just need to verify any high/critical findings and see your disclosed remediation timelines. A couple of clarifying points from our side:

- SOC 2: in progress, we have the readiness audit completed and targeting Type II by end of year.
- HIPAA: We are a covered entity for some flows; need clear controls around data-in-transit/storage, and proof of key management integration.
- Vendor questionnaire: we will send a short SIG-lite today; ideally we get the pen report and vuln SLA before completing the legal paperwork.

Rajesh — can you confirm if redacted PDF is sufficient or if you need raw scan output (Nessus/Qualys) as well?

Best,
Sylvia
Head of IT Security | MedSync
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:20:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Qualifying security posture & pen test handoff - MedSync

Rajesh — looping you in as requested. Karthik is our product-security lead; Monica (security ops) will handle the actual report handoff and SLA details. Monica, quick context: MedSync is requesting redacted pen test output and confirmation of our vuln management SLA (triage and remediation windows), scanning cadence (internal/third-party), and our disclosure process for customer-reported findings.

Ask: can you provide a brief note on the SLA cadence and a redacted report we can share?

Thanks,
Dylan
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.k@medsync.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sylvia Conrad <sylvia.conrad@medsync.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Qualifying security posture & pen test handoff - MedSync

Hi Rajesh / team —

Thanks for the intro. Short answers up front: 

- Pen test report: attaching a redacted PDF (redwood_pen_report_v2.pdf) that removes customer-identifying data and internal IP addresses. That should be sufficient for initial review. If you need raw scanner output we can provide a CSV/JSON export under an NDA.
- SLA (vulnerability management): our current public SLA is: Critical: acknowledge within 1 business hour, mitigation plan within 48 hours; High: acknowledge within 4 business hours, mitigation plan within 5 business days; Medium/Low: triage within 5 business days.
- Scanning cadence: external third-party full pentest annually, quarterly authenticated vuln scans (internal), weekly external unauthenticated scans for perimeter changes. We also run daily agent-based tech debt checks in staging.
- Disclosure / responsible disclosure: we have a 90-day remediation window for non-critical findings and a coordinated disclosure process — we will notify customers for any findings affecting customer data; we do not publish PII in reports.

Attachments included: redwood_pen_report_v2.pdf (redacted), vuln_handling_playbook.md (markdown)

Let me know if you want a short call between our SecOps and your engineering team to walk the report. Happy to set up a 30-min deep dive this week.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Security Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_pen_report_v2.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: vuln_handling_playbook.md (text)]
From: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.k@medsync.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sylvia Conrad <sylvia.conrad@medsync.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Qualifying security posture & pen test handoff - MedSync

Monica / Dylan —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the redacted report. A few action items from our side after an initial skim: 

1) Redacted PDF is fine for the procurement/legal review. We may request raw scanner output (Nessus CSV) if we get to security validation. Please confirm NDA template — we can sign Redwood's or provide ours.
2) SLA windows look reasonable; can you confirm the escalation path and POC for Critical incidents (name + phone)?
3) Would like a short 30-min SecOps sync to walk through two high findings flagged in the report and expected timelines for fixes. Our availability: Thu 25 Mar 09:00-12:00 ET or Fri 26 Mar 14:00-17:00 ET.

If you can confirm the POC and send the NDA link, we'll move the questionnaire forward and share the SIG-lite.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Security Engineering Lead | MedSync
